title: Frontend: BMI Calculator
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind BMI Calculator. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Export App. Weight is kilograms, Height is centimetres. Both must be finite and positive. Return BMI rounded to two decimal places as a string, or show Invalid measurements. This is educational arithmetic, not a diagnosis. Render controlled labelled inputs with these exact names: Weight, Height. A Calculate submit button computes the result. Render JSON.stringify(result) in [data-testid="result"]. Validation failure clears result and shows the documented message in [data-testid="error"].
constraints: Export default App. Only react and react/jsx-runtime imports are supported. The DOM contract and supplied props define the exercise.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Validate finite positive height and mass, convert height to metres, and compute mass divided by height squared.
alternativeApproaches: Add unit-preserving conversions so switching units does not silently reinterpret the same raw number.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Zero height; negative mass; centimetre conversion.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
